summary: Three test files: FunnelEventServiceTest (Mockito unit, all backstops + fan-out + keyword + error-isolation), FunnelEventServiceIT (embedded Mongo, each trigger type + fan-out + depth/fanout Redis-down + volume fail-open, doubles as bean-graph boot check), SubscriberServiceImplTest (anti-IDOR findById). Every TDD-anchor item is covered. Assertions are real (execution rows / captured enrollDepth values / WARN markers via ListAppender), not bare mock-call checks. One coverage gap worth a test.

findings.finding: The per-funnel re-enter interplay in insertOneFunnel is not directly tested: (a) allowReEnter=true funnel -> cancelExistingForPair then insert; (b) allowReEnter=false funnel raising DuplicateKeyException is swallowed and does NOT abort the rest of the fan-out (one dup must not skip sibling matches). Edge case explicitly called out in the task ('Re-enter guard interplay').
findings.recommendation: Add a unit test: two matched funnels, the first insert throws DuplicateKeyException -> the second funnel still gets inserted (verify times(1) on the second, LOG_DISPATCH_REENTER_IGNORED logged). Optionally a test that allowReEnter=true triggers cancelExistingForPair before insert.

findings.finding: Several unit tests assert via verify(executionFactory...) invocation counts. For a fan-out dispatcher this count IS the observable behavior, and the IT asserts the real persisted rows/depths — so the unit-level mock-count assertions are justified (not the 'tests only that mock was called' anti-pattern, since enrollDepth values are captured and asserted).

notes: Test-pyramid balance is correct (unit-heavy logic + targeted IT for persistence/wiring). No redundant tests. Redis-down cases spy StringRedisTemplate rather than stopping the shared container — correct per project convention.
